title: Introduce cohorted performance profiles and contextual changelog composer
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding a single model often produces a single 'global' performance profile that hides variance across customer workloads. This PR adds cohort-aware profiling, signs manifests with a lightweight provenance seal, and wires a contextual changelog composer that generates human-friendly impact blurbs for model version releases.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a cohort sampling step to the profile ingestion pipeline: profiles are now grouped by workload cohort (latency-sensitive, batch-heavy, short-seq, long-seq) using telemetry heuristics and deterministic bucketing.
- Persists multiple performance profiles per model version (cohort keys + canonical baseline). Each profile contains throughput/latency histograms, token-cost estimates, KV cache behavior summary, and recommended quantization/optim settings for that cohort.
- Introduces a provenance_seal field and signing hook to model manifests so downstream tooling can assert which profile set was computed and by which pipeline run (timestamp + short sig).
- Adds the 'contextual-changelog-composer' microservice: given two model manifests (old/new) and a small set of representative cohort profiles, it synthesizes short release notes with concrete impact statements (e.g., "-5% latency at p50 for latency-sensitive cohort; estimated -2% token cost for batch-heavy workloads"). Composer outputs both machine-friendly JSON lines and a human-optimized paragraph for release notes.
- Exposes a new CLI: `regctl profile diff --from v1.3 --to v1.4 --cohort latency-sensitive --brief` which returns the composer brief.

Implementation notes / files touched:
- ingestion/cohort_sampler.py: new deterministic bucketing and sampling logic. Uses reservoir sampling per cohort to keep sketches small.
- storage/profile_store.py: schema updated to store profile sets keyed by model_version/cohort. Backfill migration included (scripts/migrations/20241121_cohort_profiles.sql).
- manifest/signing.py: lightweight HMAC based seal using KMS-encrypted key (no key material shipped in this PR).
- composer/contextual_changelog.py: core composer logic with heuristics for impact language and numeric delta normalization.
- cli/regctl/profile.py: exposes diff/composer integration and output format flags.
- tests/*: unit tests for bucketing, composer sanity examples, integration test that runs end-to-end on a small sample profile dataset.

Backward compatibility / migration:
- Older consumers expecting a single 'performance_profile' field will still find a 'baseline' entry in the manifest to preserve compatibility. New consumers can read cohorted profiles via the profile_set key.
- Migration script is included to convert existing profile blobs into a baseline cohort; it is idempotent and guarded by a feature flag in the storage layer.

Testing & validation:
- Unit test coverage added for sampling, signing, and composer heuristics.
- Integration test runs a synthetic telemetry file through ingestion and verifies generated composer brief matches golden snapshots.
- Perf canary: a small run on staging models validated that per-cohort p99 latency change is correctly reported and within expected numerical tolerances.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy migration as feature-flagged behind `cohort_profiles_enabled` (default off).
2) Enable ingestion + storage writes for a subset of models and run composer in dry mode to accumulate examples.
3) Enable CLI outputs and invite platform teams to dogfood.
4) Gradually flip feature flag globally, monitor canary metrics and composer noise.

Checklist:
- [x] Cohort sampler implementation and unit tests
- [x] Profile_store schema + migration script
- [x] Manifest sealing hook
- [x] Contextual changelog composer + human brief template
- [x] CLI integration and docs stub
- [x] Integration tests and perf canary

Dependencies / follow-ups:
- We will follow up with a lightweight UI card in the Console to show per-cohort comparisons (ticket: ENG-9142).
- Further work to align composer language with product marketing guidelines and translation is tracked in ENG-9201.

Notes on security: the signing hook uses project KMS and rotates keys via regular rotations. No plaintext keys in repo. The migration script has a dry-run option to avoid accidental writes in early rollout.

References: Linear ENG-9142, ENG-9201. Regression risks mitigated by baseline-preservation fallback and feature flag gating.

release_notes: Add cohort-aware performance profiles and a contextual changelog composer. Manifests are now sealed with a provenance tag; CLI exposes `regctl profile diff` to generate brief release statements. Opt-in via feature flag; includes migration script.
review_comments: Diego Morales (review): Could we make the cohort bucketing deterministic across runs? Current randomness will make diffs noisy in rollouts. Reply: Yes — sampler uses a seed derived from model_version + cohort key; updated implementation ensures determinism.

Hannah Lee (review): The composer language sometimes overstates percent deltas when sample sizes are tiny. Suggest adding a minimum-sample threshold and CI guard. Reply: Added a `min_sample_count` heuristic and the composer emits a 'low-sample' note instead of a numeric delta when threshold not met.

Priya Srinivasan (review): Migration SQL needs a dry-run mode; also please ensure the baseline key is preserved for older consumers. Reply: Migration script added with `--dry-run` flag and we preserve previous 'baseline' pointer in manifest for compatibility.
